Standard Poodle.description: The first and largest breed of poodle, first bred as hunting companions. They are thin with a curly coat of fur, at least 15 inches tall, and weigh 40-70 pounds on average.

Miniature Poodle.description: The much smaller counterpart of standard poodles, only 10-15 inches tall and the same number of pounds. They have a wide variety of colors and are a popular choice as apartment companions.

Toy Poodle.description: The newest breed of poodle, developed in the 20th century. They weigh just 4-6 pounds and are under 10 inches tall. You frequently see them riding around in their owners' handbags.

English Water Spaniel.description: The English Water Spaniel is a breed of dog that has been extinct since the first part of the 20th century, with the last specimen seen in the 1930s. It was best known for its use in hunting waterfowl and for being able to dive as well as a duck.

Salish Wool Dog.description: An extinct breed of white, long-haired, Spitz-type dog that was developed and bred by the Coast Salish peoples of what is now Washington state and British Columbia for textile production.

Fuegian dog.description: The Fuegian dog is an extinct type of canine. The Fuegian dog was bred and domesticated from the South American culpeo, also known as the culpeo fox.

Hare Indian Dog.description: The Hare Indian dog is an extinct domesticated canine; possibly a breed of domestic dog, coydog, or domesticated coyote; formerly found and originally bred in northern Canada by the Hare Indians for coursing.

Chiribaya Dog.description: The Chiribaya Dog is an ancient pre-Columbian breed of dog from the southwest of Peru. It has been established that it is a llama herding dog.

Welsh Sheepdog.description: Welsh Sheepdogs are normally bred for their herding abilities rather than appearance, and so they are generally somewhat variable in build, colour and size.

Border Collie.description: The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size. It originates in the region of the Anglo-Scottish border, and descends from the traditional sheepdogs once found all over the British Isles..

Welsh Hillman.description: The Welsh Hillman was thought to have been descended from ancient Welsh herding dogs. It was possibly the oldest Welsh sheepdog, and may have been the descendant of the old gellgi or Welsh wolfhounds used around 1,000 years ago.

Cumberland Sheepdog.description: The Cumberland sheepdog is an extinct dog breed related to the border collie and other old working collie types.

Halls Heeler.description: The Halls Heeler is the presumed ancestor of two present-day dog breeds, the Australian cattle dog and the Australian stumpy tail cattle dog.

Cur.description: The cur, also called the drover's dog, was a distinct breed of dog used by cattle drovers; they are now extinct.

African Hairless Dog.description: African hairless dogs were hairless dogs from Africa. It is unknown if any examples still exist.

Alaunt.description: This type of dog may have been developed by the Alans, and was renowned primarily for its quality as a large-game catch dog, and as a war dog and guard dog.

Alpine Mastiff.description: The Alpine mastiff was a type of molosser, or flock-guardian phenotype with the same or similar ancestral origins as the Saint Bernard.

Belgian Mastiff.description: The Belgian Mastiff was a breed of mastiff-type dog from the Low Countries that was used as a draught dog.

Bullenbeisser.description: An extinct breed of dog known for its strength and agility. It is an ancestor of both the modern Boxer and the English bulldog.

Dogo Cubano.description: The Dogo Cubano, also called the Cuban Bloodhound or Cuban Bullmastiff, is an extinct Cuban breed of domestic dog. It was of the dogo sub-type of the bullmastiff dog type, which as a general class was used for bull-baiting and dog fighting.

Cordoba Fighting Dog.description: They were purposely bred for the sport of dog fighting until the early 20th century. They became extinct after dog fighting became illegal in Argentina in 1954.

Terceira Mastiff.description: The Terceira Mastiff came from the island of Terceira, located in the Azores, which is the only island where this dog has ever existed and where it was employed as a house guardian.

Argentine Polar Dog.description: The Argentine polar dog is an extinct breed of dog. It was created by the Argentine Army to haul freight around its bases in Antarctica.

Black and Tan Terrier.description: The Black and Tan Terrier was a broad breed or type of terrier that was one of the earliest terrier breeds. Although it is now extinct, it is believed to be the ancestor of all modern Fell Terrier breeds and the Welsh Terrier.

English White Terrier.description: The English White Terrier is an extinct breed of dog. English White Terrier is the failed show ring name of a pricked-ear form of the white fox-working terriers that have existed in Great Britain since the late 18th century.

Braque Dupuy.description: The Braque Dupuy, also known as the Dupuy Pointer, was a breed of pointer from the Poitou region of France. It is believed to be extinct.

Basset Hound.description: The Basset Hound is a short-legged breed of scent hound. The Basset Hound was developed in Great Britain from several now-extinct strains of French basset breeds.

Buckhound.description: The Buckhound was a breed of scent hound from England; they were used to hunt fallow deer in packs.

Grand Fauve de Bretagne.description: The Grand Fauve de Bretagne was a breed of scenthound from Brittany used to hunt wolves and wild boar.

King's White Hound.description: The King's White Hound, the Chien Blanc du Roi in French, was a breed of scent hound from France that is now extinct. The breed was said to be the favourite of the French kings from Louis XI to Louis XIV.

Chien-gris.description: The Chien-gris is an extinct breed of dog which originated in Medieval times. It was a scent hound, and formed part of the royal packs of France, which were composed, from about 1250 till 1470, exclusively of hounds of this type.

Golden Retriever.description: The Golden Retriever is a Scottish breed of retriever dog of medium-large size. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.

Labrador Retriever.description: The Labrador Retriever, also known simply as the Labrador or Lab, is a British breed of retriever gun dog.

Dalbo Dog.description: The Dalbo dog (Dalbohund) or Dalsland Mastiff is an extinct livestock guardian dog breed from Sweden.

Chow Chow.description: The Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China. The Chow Chow is a sturdily built dog, square in profile, with a broad skull and small, triangular, erect ears with rounded tips.

Cretan Hound.description: The Kritikos Lagonikos is a breed of hunting dog from the Greek island of Crete.

Zerdava.description: The Zerdava is an aboriginal laika dog breed native to the Black Sea region of Turkey and Georgia. Zerdava are traditionally used as guard and hunting dogs and are especially prized for boar hunting.

Hawaiian Poi Dog.description: The Hawaiian Poi Dog (Hawaiian: ʻīlio or ʻīlio mākuʻe) is an extinct breed of pariah dog from Hawaiʻi which was used by Native Hawaiians as a spiritual protector of children and as a source of food.

Kurī.description: The Kurī is an extinct breed of Polynesian Dog kept by Māori people. It was introduced to New Zealand by the Polynesian ancestors of the Māori during their migration from East Polynesia in the 13th century AD. According to Māori tradition, the demigod Māui transformed his brother-in-law Irawaru into the first dog.

Dumfriesshire hound.description: Dumfriesshire Black and Tan Foxhounds were a pack of foxhounds kennelled at Glenholm Kennels, Kettleholm, near Lockerbie until they were disbanded in 2001.

Mecahound.description: This dog is built out of steel and titanium.

Martian Dog.description: Martain dogs are from Mars. Duh!

5D Retriever.description: Retrieves game from the 4th and 5th dimension
